title: Sadhaura Seized and the Pir Exposed

blocks.text: At Sadhaura, Banda rejects the authority of the local pir and orders the city taken. The source contrasts homes marked for protection with households connected to the hostile establishment, which are punished as part of the campaign.

The pir’s corpse, believed by many to resist burning beneath its bier and coffin, is pulled down and consigned to fire. The scene publicly challenges the sanctity claimed around the local shrine and its defenders.
This page makes Sadhaura both punitive and symbolic: the town is seized, the pir is exposed, and the campaign is narrated as a breaking of hostile authority as well as enemy power.
